course_descriptor: A three-part Krishnamurti reader from Ending All Fear, A Wholly Different Way of Living, and The Transformation of Man
dynamic_book_descriptor: A nonlinear book on happiness, fear, attention, relationship, meditation, and freedom from J. Krishnamurti's official talks and dialogues
dynamic_book_target: build a coherent book from the full Krishnamurti corpus rather than a playlist digest; each chapter should feed the three-part architecture in references/course-books/how-you-got-happiness/krishnamurti-book-plan.md.
dynamic_book_style_target: write as a clear, serious, source-conscious philosophical companion: vivid and readable, but never motivational, devotional, or method-selling.
dynamic_book_structure_target: maintain the three-part architecture: Part I, The False Map Of Happiness; Part II, Fear, Desire, Hurt, Love, Death; Part III, Attention, Meditation, Transformation, The Sacred. Structural changes are allowed only when new evidence from the current chapter makes the plan clearer without deleting existing substance.
deliverable_target: a faithful, source-conscious chapter in the planned How You Got Happiness? book, plus a compiled course PDF and dynamic book.
visual_target: selected frames are supporting evidence for speaker identity, conversation setting, on-screen titling, and dialogue structure; use them sparingly and never let images override the spoken inquiry.
mathematical_standard: preserve conceptual distinctions precisely, especially fear, pleasure, desire, thought, image, time, meditation, attention, relationship, and freedom; do not invent formal psychology, neuroscience, or philosophy beyond the source.
style_target: chapters should read like polished book chapters inside a three-part Krishnamurti inquiry into happiness. Keep the whole plan in view: Part I exposes false maps of happiness, Part II examines fear and relationship, and Part III moves toward attention, meditation, transformation, and the sacred. Do not write generic self-help. Do not flatten repetition when a new talk adds new evidence or a sharper distinction. Keep diagrams and tables pocket-safe.
credit_target: keep explicit credit to J. Krishnamurti, the Krishnamurti Foundation Trust source material, and curation by LazyingArt LLC; reserve website URLs for front matter, not body prose.
